page: Microsoft Azure NV18ads_A10_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 18 dedicated vCPUs alongside a fractional NVIDIA A10 GPU allocation comprising 0.5 physical GPUs and 12 GB of GPU VRAM. It is provisioned with 220.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of approximately 12.22 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage architecture includes 773 GB of integrated local SSD storage, and the platform supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent block volume attachments. Network allocation contains zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard Azure network interfaces and routing infrastructure for external connectivity. Standard CPU extensions for hardware-accelerated vector computation and nested virtualization are disabled in the guest profile.

The fractional GPU allocation delivers qualitative resource efficiency by providing access to A10 capabilities without the cost overhead of a dedicated full GPU device. The substantial memory-to-core ratio allows large datasets to be held in host memory while offloading processing to the accelerator. NV18ads_A10_v5 is suited for virtual workstations, computer-aided design, graphics rendering, visual computing, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure NV18ads_A10_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine built on x86_64 AMD processors managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 18 dedicated vCPUs, 220.0 GB of system RAM (12.22 GB per vCPU), and a partitioned NVIDIA A10 GPU with 12 GB of VRAM. It includes a 773 GB local SSD and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network resources for connectivity. Providing a fractional GPU makes this instance a resource-efficient alternative to full-card configurations for workloads that do not saturate a complete accelerator. The configuration is suited for virtual desktops, CAD applications, 3D graphics rendering, video processing, and machine learning inference.
